policies.title: Your own words
policies.text: YouTube doesn't pay for reused content: videos made mostly of someone else's work, or that only read out text you didn't write, like a web page. The facts can come from Wikipedia; the script has to be yours.

policies.title: Not mass-produced
policies.text: YouTube doesn't pay for inauthentic content: mass-produced or repetitive videos, videos that look made from one template with little change, or slideshows and scrolling text with little or no story. Change the hook, footage and pacing from video to video.

policies.title: Say when AI made it look real
policies.text: Turn on YouTube's altered or synthetic content setting when a video shows realistic people, places or events made or changed with AI, like a real person seeming to say something they didn't, or AI footage of a real place. AI help with your script or captions doesn't need it.

policies.title: Music and footage you can use
policies.text: Use only music and footage you have the rights to: the music track made with your video here, YouTube's Audio Library (some tracks ask for credit), Pexels clips (free to use), or your own.

policies.title: Credit the facts
policies.text: Facts here come from Wikipedia. Put the page link in your description. Write the script in your own words: Wikipedia's text is CC BY-SA 4.0, which asks for credit and the same license if you reuse its sentences.

sponsors.title: YouTube: mark paid promotion
sponsors.text: When a video has a paid promotion, say so as you upload: Show more, then Paid promotion, then choose that your video includes branded content. Viewers see a paid promotion label when the video starts.

sponsors.title: TikTok: turn on the content disclosure
sponsors.text: Before you post a sponsored video, turn on the commercial content disclosure setting. TikTok labels the post as branded content. Sponsored posts don't earn from Creator Rewards.

sponsors.title: Say it in the video too
sponsors.text: Tell viewers in the video itself, out loud and on screen, with plain words like "ad" or "sponsored", near the start. Don't count on the platform's label alone, and don't bury it in the description.
